lesson.title: 1. Music and Nostalgia
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Chloe is helping her friend Sam* ***clear out*** *his old bedroom at his parents' house. Sam finds a box under the bed.*
lines: Oh, look what I've found. My old MP3 player. It's been under the bed for years.
That **brings back memories**. Does it still work?
Let me charge it… Yes, it does! All the songs are from about 2010.
Go on, **hit play**. **For old times' sake.**
OK, this one. I **had it on repeat** for the whole of my last year at school. I still **know every word by heart**.
I remember this! It was **all over the radio** that year. It's so **catchy**. It used to **get stuck in my head** for days.
Very. But I still love it. We used to sing it **at the top of our lungs** on the school bus.
It's funny. I haven't heard it in years, but it **takes me back**. I can still remember the smell of the school canteen.
To be honest, I think I miss that time more than the song. **Life was so much simpler.** No rent, no deadlines.
Although I complained about exams all the time!
We all did. My dad always says **they don't make music like they used to**.
I know. I've started saying it too. It **makes me feel old**.
Some of these songs are still great, though. They've **stood the test of time**.
So, are you going to throw it away?
No, I'll **keep it**. Everyone needs **a bit of nostalgia** sometimes.

lesson.title: 2. Fans and indie music
lesson.context: ***Context:*** *Mia and Jack are colleagues. It’s Monday morning, and Mia looks very tired.*
lines: You look tired today. Busy weekend?
Not really. I **stayed up late** last night trying to get concert tickets. The website **kept crashing**, but I got two **in the end**. They're right at the back, but I'm just happy to go.
Is this for that boy band you really like?
Yes, **that's the one**. I know it sounds a bit silly.
It's not silly, but **I don't really get it**. Is it really **worth losing sleep over**?

For me, yes. It's not just about the music. A few years ago, I was **going through a hard time** at work, and their songs really **got me through it**. I've also made some close friends in the **fan community**.
So it's more about the people than the band.
**Kind of.** It gives me **a sense of belonging**. When the whole stadium sings together, you **feel like part of something bigger**. It's **hard to explain**.
That sounds nice, actually. I'm just **not a big fan of** crowds. I prefer small **gigs**.
Right, you're more **into** indie music, aren't you?
Yeah. I like finding bands **before they get famous**. At small gigs, there are only about thirty people in the room, and you can hear every word. It's easy to **lose yourself in the music**.
And the songs are about real life, like paying rent or not knowing what to do with your life. The words really **speak to me**.
Sometimes. But it's **comforting** to know someone else feels the same way.
**Funnily enough**, that's exactly how I feel about my band. We just like different music.
Maybe we're **not so different after all**.

head: Purposes

homework.title: Part 3: Listening
homework.intro: Listen to a short radio talk about music and memory, then do Parts A and B.
homework.podcast: 🎧 Why old songs stay with us

script.text: Do you remember the songs you loved as a teenager? Even if you don't listen to them now, they probably still feel special. That's very normal. ==Most people remember songs from their teenage years better than songs from any other time in their life==.

Why? Because when we're teenagers, ==so many things happen for the first time==: our first best friend, our first love, our first time away from home. Our feelings are very strong, and ==the songs we hear become connected to those feelings==. So when an old song comes on, we don't just hear the music. We remember who we were.

Here's my story. When I was fifteen, ==I loved a boy band==. I had their posters all over my bedroom wall, and I waited six hours in a queue to see them in concert. ==Now I'm thirty, and I listen to jazz==. I almost never listen to that band. But last month, ==I was sitting in a café==, and one of their songs came on. ==Suddenly, I felt fifteen again==. I could almost smell my old school bag!

Experts say it doesn't really matter if a song is good or not. Some of our favourite old songs are not very good at all! ==What matters is when we heard them==. That's also why our parents often say music was better in their day.
So next time someone laughs at your old playlist, don't say sorry. It's not just a playlist. ==It's like a diary.==
